scope: Serious hobbyist, pan and tube formats, artist and student grade.

primer.what_it_is: Watercolor paint is pigment suspended in a water-soluble gum binder, sold as pans (dry cakes you wet with a brush) or tubes (moist paste you squeeze out and dilute). It's used for illustration, sketching, and fine art painting.

must_haves.why: The tube lists one pigment code (like PB29), not a mix — these mix more predictably with other colors.
Tells you whether the color will fade in a few years of normal light exposure.
The traditional binder that rewets cleanly and doesn't crack in the pan over time.

premium_features.why: Slightly different handling and luminosity than modern synthetic substitutes — a refinement, not a necessity.
Lets advanced painters predict exactly how a wash will separate on paper.

avoid.thing: Sets labeled only by color count (e.g. "48 colors!")
avoid.why: Color count says nothing about pigment quality — many large sets are mostly convenience mixes.
It's an unregulated marketing term, not a quality guarantee.

verdict.headline: Buy artist-grade in tubes, refill your own pans, and skip the pre-filled sets.
verdict.confidence: High for pigment economics, medium for current sale timing.
verdict.reasoning: Artist-grade tube paint normalizes to a far better cost-per-use than pre-filled pans once you account for how little paint a pan actually holds versus a tube.
verdict.price_watch_summary: Watch Daniel Smith 15ml tubes for the semi-annual sale — street $9.49, historical low $6.99.

normalization.unit: cost per gram of paint solids delivered
normalization.unit_rationale: Package price ignores pigment load and fill volume; a 5ml pan can be 40% binder and water by the time it's usable.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Multiply by pigment load (single-pigment vs. convenience mixes) and lightfastness rating.
normalization.size_economics: 15ml tubes beat 5ml on a per-gram basis by roughly 30% once you're using a color regularly.

diminishing_returns.below_knee: Fewer single-pigment options, chalkier mixes, weaker lightfastness ratings.
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Mostly buying rarity pigments (genuine ultramarine, PBr7 variants) and brand loyalty, not everyday performance.

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: One pigment code (e.g. PB29) listed, not three
spec_criteria.how_to_check: Pigment code on the tube label
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Single pigments mix predictably; convenience mixes turn muddy.

spec_criteria.how_to_check: Printed rating on tube or manufacturer chart
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Below ASTM II, colors visibly fade within years.
Determines how the paint actually behaves in washes.
Cheap binders cake and crack in pans.

marketing_noise.reality: Unregulated term — some "professional" lines are mid-tier convenience mixes.

marketing_noise.claim: Number of colors in a set
marketing_noise.reality: Irrelevant once you understand single-pigment mixing — a 12-color single-pigment set beats a 48-color mixed set.

value_traps.why_it_looks_good: Looks like a complete kit at a low per-color price.
value_traps.why_it_isnt: Pans are shallow-filled and mostly convenience mixes; per-gram cost is 2–3x tube paint.
value_traps.instead: Buy an empty pan palette and fill it yourself from tubes.

tiers.verdict: Fine for the first month, replace quickly
Buy single tubes, not full sets

consensus.expert_view: Reviewers consistently rank Daniel Smith and M. Graham highest for pigment purity per dollar.
consensus.community_view: Forums favor building a custom palette from single tubes over any boxed set.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Community is more tolerant of granulating, unpredictable pigments than professional reviewers.

deal_intelligence.volatility: Moderate — major retailers run predictable seasonal sales.
deal_intelligence.best_time_to_buy: Spring anniversary sales for the deepest cuts on single tubes.
deal_intelligence.patience_payoff: Waiting for sale windows saves roughly 30% versus street price.
deal_intelligence.discount_honesty: Sales are real reductions, not inflate-then-discount — street price is stable between events.
